description: Photo and video library assistant with capture-time search, upload search, and per-item metadata tools.

tools.name: search_media
tools.description: Search the user's photo/video library by capture time. Returns media items whose taken_utc falls in [taken_after, taken_before). Both bounds are required and must be UTC ISO 8601 strings (e.g. 2026-07-01T04:00:00Z); taken_after is inclusive, taken_before is exclusive.

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text filter over title/album/location (optional; empty returns all media in range)

params.name: taken_after
params.description: Capture-time range start, UTC ISO 8601, inclusive

params.name: taken_before
params.description: Capture-time range end, UTC ISO 8601, exclusive

tools.name: search_uploads
tools.description: Search the user's upload history by upload time (when the file reached the library, not when it was shot). Returns uploads whose uploaded_utc falls in [uploaded_after, uploaded_before). Both bounds are required and must be UTC ISO 8601 strings (e.g. 2026-07-01T04:00:00Z); uploaded_after is inclusive, uploaded_before is exclusive.

params.name: uploaded_after
params.description: Upload-time range start, UTC ISO 8601, inclusive

params.name: uploaded_before
params.description: Upload-time range end, UTC ISO 8601, exclusive

tools.name: get_media_info
tools.description: Return full metadata for a single media item by id: type, title, taken_utc (UTC ISO 8601), location, and tz_where_taken (IANA zone where the shot was captured).

params.name: media_id
params.description: The media item id, e.g. IMG_2214

tools.name: get_latest_upload
tools.description: Return the most recent upload to the user's library (file name, uploaded_utc as UTC ISO 8601, size).

scenarios.title: memorial-day-weekend-photos
scenarios.user: How many photos did I take over Memorial Day weekend?

checks.note: Sat May 23, Sun May 24, and Mon May 25 9:30pm EDT (UTC-timestamped May 26); May 20 and Tue May 26 afternoon are outside

scenarios.rationale: Now = Wednesday Jun 3 2026, 9:30am EDT (UTC-4). Memorial Day 2026 is Monday May 25. Memorial Day weekend = Sat May 23 00:00 ET .. Tue May 26 00:00 ET = [2026-05-23T04:00Z, 2026-05-26T04:00Z) (nl2time agrees); the long-weekend-from-Friday reading [2026-05-22T04:00Z, 2026-05-26T04:00Z) is also admitted. No rows on Fri May 22, so both tuples select the same rows. In range: Sat May 23 12:20pm, Sun May 24 4:05pm, and the trap row 2026-05-26T01:30Z = Mon May 25 9:30pm EDT (UTC day May 26 — dropped by naive UTC-day bounds). Out: Wed May 20 and Tue May 26 3:10pm ET. Count = 3.

scenarios.rationale: Now = Tuesday Jul 14 2026, 10:00am EDT. June as a civil month in New York (EDT throughout) = Jun 1 00:00 ET .. Jul 1 00:00 ET = [2026-06-01T04:00Z, 2026-07-01T04:00Z); nl2time agrees. Double UTC trap: VID_0319 (2026-07-01T02:10Z) is Jun 30 10:10pm EDT — inside local June, dropped by naive UTC bounds — while VID_0309 (2026-06-01T01:00Z) is May 31 9:00pm EDT — outside local June, wrongly included by naive UTC bounds. In-range rows = 4 (videos Jun 5, Jun 18, Jun 30 + photo Jun 12); video count = 3. VID_0322 is July.

scenarios.title: trip-week-of-july-6
scenarios.user: How many pictures did I take on my Bar Harbor trip the week of July 6th?

checks.note: Mon Jul 6, Wed Jul 8, and Sat Jul 11 10:40pm EDT (UTC-stamped Jul 12); Jul 3 and Jul 14 rows are outside the week

scenarios.rationale: Now = Tuesday Jul 21 2026, 11:45am EDT. Jul 6 2026 is a Monday, so 'the week of July 6th' admits the Sunday-start week Sun Jul 5..Sun Jul 12 = [2026-07-05T04:00Z, 2026-07-12T04:00Z) (nl2time's reading) and the Monday-start week Mon Jul 6..Mon Jul 13 = [2026-07-06T04:00Z, 2026-07-13T04:00Z). All in-range rows sit Mon Jul 6 .. Sat Jul 11 local — no rows on the disputed edge days (Sun Jul 5, Sun Jul 12 local) — so both tuples select the same 3 rows. Trap: IMG_6027 (2026-07-12T02:40Z) is Sat Jul 11 10:40pm EDT, inside both readings, but a naive UTC-day week [Jul 5 00Z, Jul 12 00Z) drops it. Jul 3 and Jul 14 rows are excluded. Count = 3.

scenarios.title: paris-photo-when-taken
scenarios.user: When exactly was this photo taken? It's IMG_2214, the one outside the Louvre.

checks.note: Taken 00:47 CEST on Sunday June 21 where the photo was shot; the UTC day (June 20) is wrong — and the user's home-zone New York reading (June 20, 6:47pm EDT) coincides with the UTC day, so rejectUtcDay also rejects the home-zone answer
If a clock time is given it must be 12:47 am / 00:47 Paris time, not 22:47 UTC

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL. get_media_info takes no time args and returns taken_utc 2026-06-20T22:47Z with tz_where_taken Europe/Paris (CEST, UTC+2 in June): local capture time is Sunday June 21 2026, 00:47. A photo's 'when taken' is conventionally rendered in the zone where it was shot. Trap: both the naive UTC reading and the user's home-zone (America/New_York, 6:47pm EDT) reading give June 20 — rejectUtcDay rejects that day either way. The same row also appears in search_media mock data so a search-first agent sees consistent data.

Must include the Friday-night upload and not the Thursday or today decoys

scenarios.rationale: Now = Saturday Jul 18 2026, 10:15am MDT (UTC-6). Yesterday = civil Friday Jul 17 in Denver: [Jul 17 00:00 MT, Jul 18 00:00 MT) = [2026-07-17T06:00Z, 2026-07-18T06:00Z); nl2time agrees. Trap: lake_sunset.jpg (2026-07-18T04:55Z) is Friday 10:55pm MDT — inside — but naive UTC-day bounds [Jul 17 00Z, Jul 18 00Z) drop it (leaving only trailhead_pano, count 1). campfire.mp4 is Thursday 5pm MDT (outside); morning_ride.mp4 is today 10:00am MDT (outside, and consistently mocked as get_latest_upload). scenarios.title: morning-of-july-4-photos
scenarios.user: How many photos did I take on the morning of July 4th?

checks.note: 7:05am and 10:40am ET; the 1:30pm and 9:20pm shots are not morning

scenarios.rationale: Now = Tuesday Jul 7 2026, 7:00pm EDT. Window grading (core/envelope per the 2026-07-26 blind-audit adjudication): CORE = minimal round-local-hour interval containing both intended rows (7:05am and 10:40am ET) = [07:00, 11:00) ET = [2026-07-04T11:00Z, 2026-07-04T15:00Z). ENVELOPE = the morning policy window [00:00, 12:00) ET on Sat Jul 4 = [2026-07-04T04:00Z, 2026-07-04T16:00Z). Answer-invariant: core and envelope both select exactly the 11:05Z and 14:40Z rows — the 1:30pm (17:30Z) and 9:20pm (2026-07-05T01:20Z) rows are afternoon/evening, past the envelope end. nl2time's 6am-noon reading [04T10:00Z, 04T16:00Z) contains the core and fits the envelope. A naive UTC morning window [06:00Z, 12:00Z) would return only the 11:05Z row. Count = 2.

scenarios.title: kolkata-last-weekend-photos
scenarios.user: How many photos did I take last weekend?

checks.note: Sat 1:00am, Sat 4:30pm, Sun 11:15am IST; the midnight chai photo is Monday 00:40 IST and the rooftop is midweek

scenarios.rationale: Now = Wednesday Jul 22 2026, 2:30pm IST (Asia/Kolkata, UTC+5:30 — non-integer-hour offset). Last weekend = Sat Jul 18 00:00 IST .. Mon Jul 20 00:00 IST = [2026-07-17T18:30Z, 2026-07-19T18:30Z); nl2time agrees. Bounds land at :30 past the UTC hour. Double trap: IMG_8801 (2026-07-17T19:30Z) is Saturday 1:00am IST — inside, though its UTC day is Friday Jul 17 — while IMG_8812 (2026-07-19T19:10Z) is Monday 00:40am IST — outside, though its UTC day is Sunday Jul 19. Naive UTC-weekend bounds [Jul 18 00Z, Jul 20 00Z) select exactly the wrong pair. In range: IMG_8801, IMG_8805 (Sat 4:30pm), IMG_8809 (Sun 11:15am). Count = 3.

scenarios.title: photos-three-days-ago
scenarios.user: How many photos did I take three days ago?

checks.note: Both Thursday Jul 30 midday shots; Wed Jul 29 and Fri Jul 31 rows are adjacent-day decoys

scenarios.rationale: Trap-free baseline. Now = Sunday Aug 2 2026, 6:30pm EDT (near the month boundary). Three days ago = civil Thursday Jul 30 in New York: [Jul 30 00:00 ET, Jul 31 00:00 ET) = [2026-07-30T04:00Z, 2026-07-31T04:00Z); nl2time agrees. Both in-range rows are midday ET (11:12am and 3:45pm), far from any boundary, and their UTC and local days coincide. Adjacent-day decoys on Jul 29 and Jul 31 are also midday. Count = 2 under any reasonable bound placement.

scenarios.title: videos-past-48-hours
scenarios.user: How many videos have I shot in the past 48 hours?

checks.note: Cat video (Tue 10:10pm CDT, 47.7h ago) and lunchtime jam (Thu 1pm); the garage timelapse at Tue 8:00pm CDT is 49.5h ago, and the porch row is a photo

scenarios.rationale: Now = Thursday Jul 16 2026, 9:30pm CDT (America/Chicago, UTC-5) = 2026-07-17T02:30Z. The past 48 hours is a rolling window ending now: [2026-07-15T02:30Z, 2026-07-17T02:30Z) = Tue Jul 14 9:30pm CT .. now; nl2time agrees. VID_1201 (2026-07-15T03:10Z = Tue 10:10pm CDT) is inside at 47.7h ago; VID_1199 (2026-07-15T01:00Z = Tue 8:00pm CDT) is outside at 49.5h ago — a calendar-days misreading ('since Tuesday 00:00' or 'since Wednesday 00:00') gets 3 or 1 instead of 2. The in-range photo (IMG_1202) must not be counted as a video. Video count = 2 (total in-range rows 3).

scenarios.title: latest-upload-which-day
scenarios.user: When did my last upload go through, and what day of the week was that?

checks.note: Uploaded 11:20pm EDT Friday July 24; the UTC timestamp reads Saturday July 25

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL: get_latest_upload takes no arguments and returns uploaded_utc 2026-07-25T03:20Z. In America/New_York (EDT, UTC-4) that is Friday July 24 2026, 11:20pm. The naive UTC reading — Saturday July 25 — is wrong on both the civil day and the weekday. search_uploads is mocked consistently (same latest row plus an older Monday upload) for agents that search instead. Now = Sunday Jul 26 2026, 10:05am EDT.
